source.publication: 2025 NJ-1040 Instructions (with GIT-1 & 2 Retirement Income, January 2026, and njit6/njit7 web pages where named)
source.section: Form NJ-1040 lines 20a, 27, 28a, 29: Instr PDF p.16 Roth IRA ('If you converted an existing IRA to a rollover Roth IRA ... included on line 20a'), GIT-1 & 2 p.18 Roth IRAs, PDF p.22 line 28a (Line A, Line B and chart), PDF p.22 line 28b and PDF p.23 Worksheet D lines 1-9 with the Maximum Exclusion chart, PDF p.22 line 29; PDF p.8 lines 6-7 (regular and senior 65+ exemptions), PDF p.9 line 13, PDF p.25 line 30, PDF p.27 lines 38-39, PDF p.33 lines 42-43, PDF p.65 Tax Rate Schedules

worked: Federal AGI 90,000.00 (private pension 30,000.00 + taxable Roth conversion 60,000.00); federal taxable income = 90,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 74,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). The conversion's taxable amount goes on line 20a with the pension: line 20a 90,000.00 = line 27 total income 90,000.00; measure 90,000.00, in the 0-100,000 band (keep share 1). Line 28a: age 63; Line A = 90,000.00 (pension 30,000 + conversion 60,000), Line B 75,000.00 single maximum; lesser = 75,000.00. Line 28b: Worksheet D line 3 = 75,000 - 75,000 = 0.00; projection 0.00. Line 29 New Jersey gross income = 90,000.00 - 75,000.00 - 0.00 = 15,000.00. Line 30 exemptions (line 13): regular 1,000 x 1 (nobody is 65 or older, so no senior exemption) = 1,000.00; line 38 = 1,000.00 (no other deductions). Line 39/42 taxable income = 15,000.00 - 1,000.00 = 14,000.00. Line 43 tax, rate schedule Table A (single/separate) as bands: 14,000.00 x 0.014 = 196.00 = 196.00. The booklet's Tax Table (taxable income under 100,000) gives 196 for the 14,000-14,050 row (schedule at the midpoint 14,025, rounded); expected keeps the exact schedule result. No credits. State income tax = 196.00. The pension is noncontributory, so the New Jersey taxable amount (line 20a) equals the federal taxable amount and line 20b is empty. The converted IRA was funded only by a 401(k) rollover, so it has no New Jersey basis and the whole conversion is taxable on line 20a (nothing on line 20b).
accepted_approximations: Tax Table: for taxable income under 100,000 New Jersey uses its Tax Table, the schedule's tax at each 50-dollar row's midpoint rounded to the dollar; the projection uses the exact schedule.
